title: MiniMax releases M3, a 428B open-weight frontier model with 1M context and native multimodality
summary: MiniMax released the MiniMax M3 open-weights model on June 12, 2026, combining a 428B-parameter mixture-of-experts architecture (23B active) with a 1M-token context window and native image-and-video understanding; the model posts 59.0% on SWE-Bench Pro, 66.0% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 74.2% on MCP Atlas, and ships with the new MiniMax Sparse Attention, a Day-0 API on platform.minimax.io, and weights on Hugging Face under a commercially permissive license.

title: Moonshot open-sources Kimi K2.7-Code with 30% fewer thinking tokens and a high-speed tier on June 15
summary: Moonshot AI released Kimi K2.7-Code on June 12, 2026 as an open-source 1T-parameter MoE (32B active) coding model with ~30% lower reasoning-token usage than K2.6, vendor-reported gains of +21.8% on Kimi Code Bench v2, +11.0% on Program Bench and +31.5% on MLS Bench Lite; weights are live on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license, a Kimi Code coding-agent launch is priced from $19/month, and a high-speed K2.7-Code variant arrives June 15 with 5–6× faster output at roughly double the API price.

title: US government orders Anthropic to suspend Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 worldwide over jailbreak claims
summary: Anthropic disclosed on June 12, 2026 that the US government issued an export-control directive at 5:21 pm ET the same day ordering the immediate shutdown of Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 for all users globally, citing a claimed 'narrow, non-universal jailbreak' of Fable 5; Anthropic complied but published a blog post disputing the evidence, warning that applying the same standard 'would essentially halt all new model deployments' across the frontier-AI industry.

title: NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra NVL72 tops the first Agentic AI infrastructure benchmark, 20× more agents per megawatt than Hopper
summary: NVIDIA announced on June 12, 2026 that its Blackwell Ultra NVL72 platform led the first round of AgentPerf from Artificial Analysis, the industry's first open, multi-vendor agentic-AI infrastructure benchmark, running up to 20× more concurrent agents per megawatt than the NVIDIA HGX H200 system on DeepSeek V4 Pro workloads at SLO=30; the result is attributed to NVFP4 quantization, fifth-gen Tensor Cores, NVLink scale-up and 288GB of HBM3e per GPU, with Baseten, DeepInfra and Together AI already serving production agentic traffic on Blackwell.

title: Mistral CEO Mensch makes the case for Vibe as Europe's enterprise agentic AI platform, hints at custom chips
summary: Mistral CEO Arthur Mensch told CNBC on June 12, 2026 that Mistral is exploring designing its own chips and that enterprise AI adoption still has a long runway; the interview doubles as a launch moment for Vibe, Mistral's agentic enterprise platform built on the 128B-parameter Mistral Medium 3.5 model with Work and Code modes, $3.1B raised to date, an $830M Paris data-center debt round, and roughly 95% of revenue from business customers.

title: Hugging Face ships Serge, an open-source GitHub-native AI code reviewer that plugs into any OpenAI-compatible model
summary: Hugging Face introduced Serge on June 12, 2026, an Apache-2.0 open-source GitHub-native AI code reviewer that talks to OpenAI-compatible chat-completion endpoints (OpenAI, the Hugging Face Router, local vLLM/TGI/LM Studio) and is already in use on the diffusers, transformers and Serge repositories themselves; reviewers can pick any model exposed by the Hugging Face Router, including freshly open-weighted models like MiniMax M3 and Kimi K2.7-Code.

title: Google researchers propose 'faithful uncertainty' to let LLMs hedge instead of hallucinating
summary: Google researchers published a new paper on June 12, 2026 introducing 'faithful uncertainty', a metacognitive technique that aligns a model's linguistic hedging ('My best guess is…') with its intrinsic statistical confidence; the authors argue this reframes hallucinations as 'confident errors' and is critical for agentic systems, where metacognition acts as the central control layer for tool calls, retrieval evaluation, and avoiding sycophantic acceptance of bad context.

title: Former xAI engineer sues SpaceX and xAI, alleging he was fired for raising Grok safety and export-control concerns
summary: Devin Kim, a former xAI engineer who left in September 2025 and is now president of the nonprofit Center for AI Safety, filed suit against xAI and SpaceX in California state court on June 12, 2026, alleging he was dismissed in retaliation for repeatedly warning that Grok could spread discrimination and weapons-related information; the complaint also claims co-founder Jimmy Ba sought to bypass EU safety testing for Grok Code 1 and ignored Musk's own directives on testing, days before SpaceX's expected record-breaking IPO.

title: Meta's three-month-old Applied AI unit is in open revolt, with engineers calling it a 'soul-crushing gulag'
summary: Wired reported on June 12, 2026 that Meta's three-month-old Applied AI organization of roughly 6,500 engineers and product managers is in revolt, with members describing the unit as 'soul-crushing' and more than 1,600 Meta employees company-wide signing a petition against a click-and-keystroke monitoring program used to train Muse Spark; Chief Product Officer Chris Cox acknowledged the 'brutal' environment on an internal call, and CEO Mark Zuckerberg followed up Friday with a memo admitting 'recent changes had caused distress' and committing to fix the mistakes.

title: Anthropic releases first Anthropic Public Record: 51,993 Americans surveyed, only 15% trust AI companies to decide for them
summary: Anthropic published the first wave of its new Anthropic Public Record survey series on June 12, 2026, drawing on a nationally representative YouGov sample of 51,993 Americans fielded from November to December 2025; 48% ranked curing diseases in their top-three hopes for AI, 64% identified AI-induced job loss as their top fear, more than 70% want government regulation, and just 15% said they trust AI companies to make decisions about how AI is developed and used.

title: Google sues suspected Chinese 'Outsider Enterprise' ring for using Gemini to build 9,000 phishing sites and 2.5M scam texts
summary: Google filed a lawsuit on June 12, 2026 against a suspected Chinese cybercrime group called the Outsider Enterprise, alleging it used Google's own Gemini chatbot to generate code for 9,000 fraudulent websites and more than one million malicious URLs, then sent over 2.5 million phishing texts to Android users in a two-week May campaign; the case is Google's second major AI-fraud suit after Lighthouse in 2025 and the first to explicitly allege generative AI as a tool in the scam supply chain.

title: Anthropic launches $15M Claude cyber defense program for state, local, tribal and territorial governments
summary: Anthropic announced a $15 million cyber defense program on June 12, 2026 that gives state, local, tribal and territorial (SLTT) governments up to $100,000 in Claude credits each to find and fix vulnerabilities using Claude Opus 4.8, Claude Security and Claude Code, plus hands-on support and weekly training from Anthropic's applied-AI team; the first cohort kicked off the same day with California and Texas signed on, and the program is distinct from the restricted-access Project Glasswing cyber initiative.

title: OpenAI acquires Ona to give Codex long-running, customer-controlled cloud execution
summary: OpenAI announced on June 11, 2026, that it will acquire Ona, a startup whose technology provides secure, persistent cloud environments where AI agents can access tools, systems, and context over time; Ona's customer-controlled execution model will let Codex agents operate inside an organization's own cloud while OpenAI provides the intelligence and orchestration, with the Ona team joining OpenAI's Codex group after closing.

title: OpenAI and Visa embed agentic payments inside ChatGPT for any merchant on the network
summary: OpenAI and Visa announced a partnership on June 11, 2026, that lets ChatGPT shop and complete purchases on behalf of users at any merchant that accepts Visa, with tokenized credentials, spending limits, required approvals, and merchant allowlists; the framework also exposes the rails to developers and merchants via OpenAI's agentic commerce protocol.

title: OpenAI ships models and Codex through Oracle Cloud, letting enterprises draw down existing commitments
summary: OpenAI announced on June 11, 2026, that its models and the Codex coding agent are now available through Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, letting enterprise customers apply existing Oracle Cloud commitments to OpenAI usage and avoid fresh procurement cycles; the arrangement turns Oracle into a first-class OpenAI distribution channel alongside Microsoft Azure.

title: Anthropic and DXC Technology form multi-year alliance to deploy Claude inside banks, airlines, and government
summary: Anthropic and DXC Technology announced a multi-year global alliance on June 11, 2026, in which DXC will train tens of thousands of Claude-certified forward-deployed engineers to bring Claude into the systems DXC operates for the world's largest banks, airlines, insurers, manufacturers, and government agencies, starting with Modernization-as-a-Service, cybersecurity, and OASIS-based application services.

title: Anthropic taps TCS to scale Claude across Indian enterprises, financial services, and Diligenta
summary: Anthropic partnered with Tata Consultancy Services on June 11, 2026, to set up a dedicated business unit for deploying Claude to TCS customers, give more than 50,000 TCS employees access to Claude, and build out Diligenta (22M+ UK life-and-pensions customers) and TCS iON on top of the Claude Code ecosystem.

title: Google DeepMind commits $10M with Schmidt Sciences, ARIA, and Cooperative AI to study multi-agent safety
summary: Google DeepMind, Schmidt Sciences, ARIA, the Cooperative AI foundation, and Google.org announced a $10 million research fund on June 11, 2026, to seed academic work on how millions of AI agents will behave when they interact across the open internet; DeepMind's AGI safety lead Rohin Shah says the field of multi-agent safety effectively does not exist yet and the timing is urgent.

title: Google releases DiffusionGemma, a 26B open diffusion language model that runs on 18GB of RAM
summary: Google DeepMind unveiled DiffusionGemma on June 11, 2026, an experimental 26-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts language model that generates paragraphs of tokens in parallel using diffusion rather than autoregressive decoding, posting up to 4x speedup on a single H100 and running locally on 18GB of DRAM or VRAM; the open-weights model is released under Apache 2.0 with vLLM, MLX, and HF Transformers support.

title: xAI launches Grok Build Plugin Marketplace with MongoDB, Vercel, Sentry, Chrome DevTools, and Cloudflare
summary: xAI launched the Grok Build Plugin Marketplace on June 11, 2026, a built-in catalog of plugins that bundle skills, slash commands, agents, hooks, MCP servers, and LSPs into a single installable package; the launch catalog ships six partners and pins every remote plugin to a 40-character commit SHA that Grok Build re-verifies after cloning.

title: NVIDIA launches Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX) for autonomous manufacturing agents
summary: NVIDIA announced the Factory Operations Blueprint, or FOX, at GTC Taipei on June 11, 2026, a reference design for building autonomous factory manager agents that connect machine data, quality systems, work instructions, robot fleets, and operational alerts into one AI-driven decision layer; the blueprint is built on NemoClaw, AI-Q Blueprint, and Nemotron open models.

title: Perplexity moves Deep Research into Computer, routing subtasks across 20+ frontier models
summary: Perplexity moved Deep Research into its Computer multi-model orchestration system on June 11, 2026, breaking hard questions into subtasks and routing them across 20+ frontier models to produce reports, decks, and dashboards; BrowseComp accuracy jumped from 40.7% to 83.8% and Humanity's Last Exam rose 36.4% to 50.5%, with Search-as-Code available through both Computer and the Agent API.

title: Zhipu launches GLM-5.1 with 8-hour autonomous work mode and 10% price hike
summary: Zhipu released GLM-5.1 with a new '8-hour work mode' that lets the model independently plan, execute, test, and self-repair across a single task, becoming the first domestic model to top Opus 4.6 on SWE-bench Pro; pricing rose 10%, reaching parity with Anthropic in coding scenarios as the company pivots from price competition to long-duration agent execution.

title: Meta's Muse Spark AI replaces Llama 4 across Ray-Ban and Oakley smart glasses
summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs extended its Muse Spark model to all Ray-Ban and Oakley smart glasses except Meta Ray-Ban Display; Muse Spark matches Llama 4 Maverick performance at 10x lower compute, is closed-source, and Meta has delayed the public API multiple times since April while targeting a release within June.
